correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts the only \(\Omega(n)=2\) shapes. For \(p^2\), divisibility forces \(2p+1\mid3\), impossible. For distinct primes \(p<q\), the condition reduces exactly to \(p+q\mid pq+1\), equivalently \(p+q\mid p^2-1\). Writing \(k=(pq+1)/(p+q)\) gives \(2\le k<p\) and the exact identity \((p-k)(q-k)=k^2-1\); both converse parametrizations are direct algebra.

value.rationale: The semiprime layer is the first composite multiplicative layer of a long-standing exact divisibility sequence. The theorem gives two finite, exact, and mutually equivalent generators—divisors of \(p^2-1\) and factor pairs of \(k^2-1\)—so membership is structurally explained rather than merely enumerated. This is a natural complete classification with a reusable quotient-fiber form.
